pages.title: Summer: props connect the merchandise
pages.body: Fishing rods, hands and folding chairs create a viewing path. Compare product position, prop scale and background contrast so the narrative keeps merchandise legible.

images.caption: Summer window with a fishing rod, folding chair, fish props and a speech bubble
Summer window with a mannequin, drink-shaped prop, orange slice and COOL speech bubble

pages.title: Autumn: familiar frames, unfamiliar scale
pages.body: Doors, windows and walls establish spatial references. Oversized animals disrupt those references while framing and suspension separate merchandise from large props.

images.caption: Autumn window with an oversized pink fish passing through a doorway beside a mannequin
Autumn window with a yellow snail, an open door and a suspended pink bag

pages.title: Winter: different rhythms for different windows
pages.body: Wide windows connect products across snow planes. Tall windows build a vertical hierarchy around the horse. Each format requires a new composition.

images.caption: Wide winter window with a large white horse head, snowy planes, a yellow bag and a small pink horse
Layered white horse contours and suspended accessories against a blue background

pages.title: From visual direction to spatial relationships
pages.body: My contribution was 3D design and visual presentation within BENWU. The retrospective diagram compares composition and merchandise hierarchy; individual production and store-delivery responsibility is not established.

images.caption: From visual direction to spatial relationships

pages.title: Terrain, body and equipment
pages.body: A rock face anchors the background, layered contours form the middle ground and a mannequin establishes human scale. Their boundaries and overlap help equipment remain readable.

images.caption: Arc’teryx Mountain Performance Field | user-supplied retrospective board 01 / 10
Arc’teryx Alpha Center window with rock forms, layered curves and a mannequin holding poles

pages.title: Communicate spatial relationships
pages.body: Compare the rock face, curves and equipment as distinct layers. Window format, lighting and product visibility guide the spatial reading.

pages.title: The window in its retail context
pages.body: Additional installation views connect the window with the interior. Rock, directional lines, mannequins and moss surfaces extend the mountain language around clothing and circulation.

images.caption: Arc’teryx Alpha Center installation, front window

pages.title: Build the system around recognition
pages.body: Compare the photography-equipment context, name recognition and small-scale legibility. The wordmark anchors the visual and information system.

images.caption: Design decisions and system applications (Chinese diagram)

pages.title: Compare the wordmark at different scales
pages.body: The PERIASTRA wordmark study, dated 9 June 2026, supports comparison of letterforms, hierarchy, application scale and production direction.

pages.title: From historical exploration to a private seal
pages.body: The earlier Songnasty exploration and current YELISI mark show a shift in identity language. Seal, folded line and cut-corner forms connect naming, graphics and product context.

pages.title: Connect identity, products and CMF
pages.body: Collaborative brand and product-concept work shares a material direction. The archive supports comparison of form and surface; no manufacture or market launch is claimed.
